title: The planning marathon - making improvements in the long run

content.text: Tom Warth (Chief Operating Officer) reflects on the Planning Inspectorate’s long-term improvements as the latest performance statistics are published.

Secretary of State for Housing, Angela Rayner, recently likened the Government’s target for new homes to running a marathon in under 5 hours – a challenge without doubt, she said, but achievable nonetheless.
It is an analogy that feels familiar- we’ve been on a journey to improve, but the hard yards, teamwork and long-term strategies have us producing good times.
I wrote recently about our own ‘marathon’ efforts to improve productivity and bring certainty into the planning process.
As I concluded then, there’s plenty still do, but our quarterly statistics published this week show those tough miles over the last few years continue to make us quicker.
Here’s what this week’s release tells us:
Of course, so much of our and your work isn’t about appeals.

More than 700 of you tuned in live to our recent webinar Plan, Prepare, Progress: A practical guide to the new local plan system, and we were inundated with questions afterwards (99 to be very precise), so we know plans are on your minds.
On the subject of new guidance, there’s plenty going on in the world of infrastructure.
Just last week a number of amendments to the Planning Act 2008 introduced by the Planning and Infrastructure Act 2025 came into force.
They affect the process of applying for, and making representations about, applications for nationally significant infrastructure projects (NSIPs).
Do have a read and of course make sure you use our pre-application service to get that vital information and feedback ahead of an application.
So, the ‘planning as marathon’ metaphor? Well, there’s certainly a marathon amount of reading to get through with all the new guidance and plenty of reform to come.

As with all long-distance races, the best outcomes happen when there is a race plan with a realistic pace. I hope you'll see from our data that, although it isn't going to happen overnight, our plan is working and the support of customers and stakeholders makes all the difference.
